title: Rate amplification for non-adaptive linear locally correctable codes via dual smooth recovery

license.name: CC BY4.0
license.adaptation_notice: Faithful editable transcription from the official CCC2021 CC BY4.0 published version, article1. One rate-amplification mechanism: introductory Theorem3 and formal Theorem46/Proposition55 with all of Sections4/4.1/4.2/4.3/4.4 author constructions and proofs, plus the full necessary Section5.2 axis-evasive partition construction and Claims57--63/Proposition60/Theorem62 proof. Definitions1--2/non-adaptive/linear code context and Claim82 retained. The unused probabilistic alternative Section5.1 is outside this item, as the author explicitly says it is not used; no separately counted support lemma. All43 original bibliography entries retained. Author wording/printed indices and equations are preserved without mathematical correction, including Definition25 distinct/not-necessarily-distinct wording, Claim23 z direction, Corollary49 final displayed little-o sign, Proposition60 final denominator c, Claim59 property numbering and final Theorem62 printed I indices. Author omitted details remain omitted rather than supplied: Fact24 called easy to verify, Claim82 induction, and Proposition55 final error calculation left to reader. These are the authors actual proofs, not extraction omissions. Formal54 parity wording retained as printed. All field/linearity/nonadaptivity/rate/error/smoothness/alphabet and prime-residue conditions retained. Root handles compilation/database/publication.

standard_prerequisites.name: Siegel-Walfisz theorem
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Original Theorem48[34,37] statement and full author Corollary49 deduction retained.

standard_prerequisites.name: Basic finite-field and cyclic-group facts
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Full Section5.2 author use and supporting calculations retained; no recursion into standard algebra.

core_obligations: Retain complete linear/non-adaptive LCC to SLR and dual-SLR equivalence chain.
Retain tensor lifting and complete distance-efficient modification/probability proofs.
Retain prime-residue projection and parameter-iteration proof of Proposition55/Theorem46.
Retain full Section5.2 axis-evasive partition construction and proof supporting the main rate-amplification result.
difficulty_reason: The author amplifies dual-SLR rate using tensor products and an axis-evasive partition correction that preserves smooth recovery; a quadratic finite-field coset construction and a prime-residue projection permit repeated amplification with controlled rate, error and smoothness. These are explicit nonroutine algebraic/combinatorial mechanisms.
